segments.text: April 30, 2024 — As recorded in the meeting minutes:

. Mr. Gagon stated he was also there with the group on the 200 South construction project. His concerns dealt with safety, signage, and oversight. He has lived here for 30 years, and he has noticed that a lot of construction projects seem to begin and then the project goes on and on with no progress being made. That seemed to be the issue in his area as well as near Rotary Park. He questioned if there was a lack of oversight. He noted there are detours on roads that seem to be fine. Mr. Gagon shared an experience where a construction truck backed into his vehicle, when there were no signs indicating where exactly the construction zone was. He made a left hand turn and immediately there was a dump truck that backed into him. There was no visual signage saying he couldn’t turn left. Had the dump truck not stopped when he did, he could have been crushed. When the driver was questioned why he didn’t look, he said it was a construction zone. This is the experience that residents have seen, and he hoped for oversight on the construction project with police possibly monitoring the construction sites to make sure appropriate signs are in place.
